title: Could our organization's voice or likeness be convincingly deep-faked, and are we ready if it is?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether an organisation has a detection and rapid-response plan for synthetic media impersonating its leadership, brand, or communications channels.
question_text: If someone used AI voice-cloning or likeness-generation to impersonate our CEO, another executive, or our brand in a convincing way — as happened with a sitting US president in the New Hampshire robocall case — how quickly would we detect it, and do we have a rapid-response plan to alert affected audiences?
rationale: The New Hampshire deepfake robocall showed that a convincing AI-cloned voice of a well-known public figure can be distributed at scale before any detection or disclosure mechanism intervenes.
follow_up_actions: Confirm whether any synthetic-media detection capability monitors channels using the organisation's brand or leadership likeness.
Establish a rapid-response communication plan for a suspected deepfake impersonation event.
Review the synthetic media disclosure log for any prior flagged incidents involving the organisation.
